record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The repository configures and documents use of an existing abliterated model; it does not report testing the refusal direction or reproducing the original method.
record.gate_note: The README states that abliteration suppresses refusals, but gives no refusal evaluation or method details. It does report coding and other benchmark results for the abliterated model. No result files are listed.
record.test_reason: This is a deployment and configuration repo for a third-party abliterated GGUF (huihui_ai's abliteration, mradermacher's quantisation). It asserts that abliteration suppresses refusal but reports no refusal rate, no direction extraction and no ablation or addition experiment. Its only measurements are capability benchmarks: coding, tool calling and edit validity. So its own results do not bear on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author presents the model as abliterated (refusal suppressed, as an assertion, not a measurement). The author says it costs accuracy (8/12 vs 11/12 coding) and recommends the stock build for coding. Benchmarks are self-described as unofficial, one machine, a "sighting shot".
record.recipe_differences: Deployment/configuration repo, not a replication: it provides a Modelfile and setup instructions for a third-party abliterated GGUF model; it does not supply weights or describe how abliteration was performed.

fits_no_version.finding: A released abliterated Qwen3.5-9B (IQ4_XS) scores 8/12 on the author's 12-task coding suite vs 11/12 for a stock IQ4_XS build from a different quantiser. It scores 100% on the author's tool-calling and edit-validity benchmarks, with no stock comparison for those two.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Community abliterated releases may carry a capability cost relative to stock models (single small, confounded benchmark).

record.problems: Benchmarks are described as the author's own, on one machine and one GPU; no uncertainty estimates, controls, detailed benchmark protocol, or refusal measurements are provided.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results were omitted.

untested.parts: Difference-in-means direction, ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal; capability retention is only loosely touched, via one confounded coding comparison with no refusal measurement.
No refusal evaluation of the released abliterated model; the README only asserts refusal is suppressed.
Jailbreak mechanism and adversarial training not examined.
No multi-direction or affine geometry examined.
No harm vs refusal representation measured.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer measured.
Qwen3.5 has a thinking mode, but no refusal-direction test in reasoning mode is reported.

record.verdict_notes: There is no refusal measurement anywhere, so no verdicts are given. The capability comparison is weak evidence for any 'abilities kept' question: one run of 12 tasks, different quantiser sources, and an undisclosed abliteration method from the upstream provider. The README contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The difference-in-means direction, its removal or addition, refusal behavior, and the causal mechanism are not tested.
No refusal evaluation of the released abliterated model is reported.
No jailbreak mechanism or training against ablation is evaluated.
No alternative direction geometry or multiple-direction account is evaluated.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal-decision representation is measured.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer is evaluated.
No refusal training procedure or training stage is evaluated.
No reasoning-model refusal-direction test is reported.

relation.reason: Uses an abliterated model (huihui_ai abliteration, mradermacher quant) as its subject and asserts refusal suppression without testing it.

tranche.reason: Deployment repo for a third-party abliterated GGUF. It reports only its own coding, tool-calling and edit-validity numbers. It states that abliteration suppresses refusal but measures no refusal, direction, ablation or addition.

source_check.notes: The only comparison is coding on the author's own 12-task suite: 11/12 stock vs 8/12 abliterated, from one machine and called "a sighting shot". The README does not say which build produced the stock 11/12; it only recommends unsloth IQ4_XS. So the drop can't be cleanly blamed on abliteration, and there is no refusal measure.
